3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Titus pushed the door open with a firm hand.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Seeing him up close, I noticed the scar that cut across his nose. His unkempt beard and rugged olive-green coat looked out of place in the polished room.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: His eyes scanned the surroundings briefly before locking onto mine.

7.speaker: Player_Romus
7.text: "Don’t you know that you must bow when your King enters?"

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: He didn't flinch. His lips curled slightly with a brief flicker of amusement.

9.speaker: Player_Romus
9.text: "I advise you to choose your next words carefully."

11.speaker: Player_Romus
11.text: "Good to see you here, House Speaker."

13.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
13.text: "I appreciate the opportunity to converse with you directly. Thank you for inviting me here."

14.speaker: Player_Romus
14.text: "To be frank, I never thought I'd be hosting a revolutionary in this palace. But these are extraordinary times."

15.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
15.text: "Indeed not. But the people's voice has grown louder, reaching ears in places it once couldn't."

16.speaker: Narrator
16.text: He smiled slightly. There was something almost disarming about the way he stood -- confident, yet ill at ease in the grandeur of our surroundings.

17.speaker: Player_Romus
17.text: "Thank you for accepting my invitation. It’s not every day that a Malenyevist and a King come together."

18.speaker: Player_Romus
18.text: "And how is everything in the House of Delegates, Mr. Speaker?"

19.speaker: Player_Romus
19.text: "I hope you are doing something to contain the unrest in the streets, Mr. Sotelato."

20.speaker: Player_Romus
20.text: "Loud or not, I am still your King."

22.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
22.text: "The Delegates have been calling for comprehensive democratic reforms for a while now. Calls that have gone unanswered."

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: Adarfo’s smile faded slightly, replaced by a serious expression.

24.speaker: Player_Romus
24.text: "It seems that voice has found a formidable representative in you, Mr. Sotelato."

28.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
28.text: "It's too late for compromise. The people are fed up with the system as it is."

29.speaker: Player_Romus
29.text: "Good to see you here, Mr. Sotelato."

33.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
33.text: "The people’s struggles are my own, Your Majesty. I've lived them."

34.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
34.text: "And now, I aim to ensure their cries will no longer go unheard."

35.speaker: Narrator
35.text: Adarfo’s smile faded slightly, replaced by a serious expression.

37.speaker: Player_Romus
37.text: "Then tell me... what *does* it look like?"

38.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
38.text: "I don't bow to relics, Romus Toras. Not anymore."

39.speaker: Player_Romus
39.text: "So... you're the man who wants to put me out of a job."

40.speaker: Player_Romus
40.text: "You are in the presence of your King. If you wish to address me, you will bow."

41.speaker: Player_Romus
41.text: "You are a guest in my palace, Adarfo. You may claim not to bow to relics, but royal tradition still matters."

42.speaker: Player_Romus
42.text: "I've seen relics survive longer than revolutions."

43.speaker: Narrator
43.text: I saw his fingers twitch, the only hint that my demand had struck a nerve.

45.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
45.text: "I prefer to think of it as dismantling the machineries of oppression."

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: He didn't so much as flinch. His lips curled slightly with a brief flicker of amusement.

47.speaker: Player_Romus
47.text: "Is that what you tell yourself? That refusing to bow furthers your cause somehow? It’s a petulant defiance, Adarfo -- a child playing at revolution."

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: I saw his fingers twitch, the only hint that my demand had struck a nerve.

49.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
49.text: "Relics become relics because they outlive their purpose."

50.speaker: Narrator
50.text: A cold smile formed on his lips.

51.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
51.text: "Tradition? It’s tradition that’s kept this country in chains. And you expect me to bow to it?"

52.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
52.text: "I stand in the presence of a man who has summoned me for a meeting. A request that I have honored by coming here."

53.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
53.text: "So let me address you as that man, because that's all you are."

54.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
54.text: "Let me address you as an equal. After all, the only difference between us is that you happen to have been born into privilege."

56.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
56.text: "And that’s all your monarchy is -- an outdated symbol. You’re a man like any other, Romus, so let me address you as an equal."

57.speaker: Player_Romus
57.text: "Address me however you like, Mr. Sotelato, but know that I'm not your enemy. Now, please take a seat."

58.speaker: Narrator
58.text: He opened his arms and gestured at our surroundings.

59.speaker: Player_Romus
59.text: "A man, yes. But a man who holds a nation together."

60.speaker: Player_Romus
60.text: "It's far easier to criticize someone's leadership than to wear the crown yourself."

61.speaker: Player_Romus
61.text: "And refusing to bow to your King is part of that quest? It’s a petulant defiance, Adarfo -- a child playing at revolution."

62.speaker: Player_Romus
62.text: "'Dismantling the machineries of oppression?' You've been reading too many manifestos."

63.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
63.text: "Criticism is what the powerless use until they’re given the tools to change the system."

64.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
64.text: "Defiance isn't childish. It’s a necessity in the face of tyranny."

65.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
65.text: "And the people are learning to stand up to those who would prefer them to prostrate themselves."

66.speaker: Narrator
66.text: He raised an eyebrow and nodded.

67.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
67.text: "You’d do well to read a few yourself. Maybe then you’d realize that they aren't mere theories, but the lived experiences of your people."

71.speaker: Player_Romus
71.text: "Relax, Adarfo. I summoned you here to listen to what you had to say, not to threaten or deride."

74.speaker: Narrator
74.text: I gestured at the empty chair beside me.

75.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
75.text: "Thank you, Your Majesty, but I'll be fine."

76.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
76.text: "Nothing theatrical about it. I simply prefer to stand when I speak for the people."

77.speaker: Narrator
77.text: He remained in place, his posture defiant.

78.speaker: Narrator
78.text: He remained in place, eyeing our surroundings.

79.speaker: Player_Romus
79.text: "I insist. We may be on opposite sides of this, but we are both capable of engaging in conversation. There’s no need for theatrics."

83.speaker: Player_Romus
83.text: "I insist. I am on your side, and we are both men capable of conversation. There’s no need for theatrics."

84.speaker: Player_Romus
84.text: "Well, suit yourself. I thought perhaps a seat might make this feel less like an interrogation."

85.speaker: Player_Romus
85.text: "If we're going to have a real conversation, I think we can both agree that mutual respect is the first step. And respect means following basic decorum."

86.speaker: Player_Romus
86.text: "You might find the conversation more productive if you sit. We’re both here to discuss the future of Rizia."

87.speaker: Player_Romus
87.text: "Fine. Stand. Like a soldier awaiting orders."

88.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
88.text: "I appreciate the thought, but I’m here to make my position clear. Sitting doesn't change what’s coming."

89.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
89.text: "Thank you, but the people I represent aren't concerned with decorum. It's just another of the chains that are binding us."

90.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
90.text: "You'll find that I'm not so easily provoked. I didn't come here to be baited into an argument."

91.speaker: Player_Romus
91.text: "So be it, Adarfo. Address me however you like. Now, please take a seat."

92.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
92.text: "If you really mean what you say, Your Majesty, I believe we can have a respectful dialogue."

93.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
93.text: "Really? Because demanding a gesture of submission right from the start sends a rather different signal."

94.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
94.text: "But if you are indeed here to listen, we can have a respectful dialogue."

98.speaker: Player_Romus
98.text: "Good. That's exactly what I want. Why don't you take a seat?"

103.speaker: Player_Romus
103.text: "I get not wanting to bow, but let’s not make this harder than it needs to be. Just sit down. We’re here to talk."

104.speaker: Player_Romus
104.text: "I might be more receptive to those ideas than you'd think."

108.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
108.text: "Intriguing words, Your Majesty. But empty without action."

110.speaker: Player_Romus
110.text: "Let's take a step back, Adarfo. I summoned you here to open up a dialogue and listen to your concerns."

111.speaker: Player_Romus
111.text: "You think that once you get rid of me and put yourself in power, everything will just fall into place?"

112.speaker: Player_Romus
112.text: "The monarchy you scorn is the same institution that has kept this nation intact through war, famine, and countless other hardships."

113.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
113.text: "But if you are indeed here to have that conversation, Your Majesty, we can have a respectful dialogue."

114.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
114.text: "It’s hard to believe that when you greet me so dismissively right from the start."

115.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
115.text: "We have a new vision for Rizia. One in which nobody wears a crown."

116.speaker: Player_Romus
116.text: "I understand what you're getting at. And I'm willing to listen."

117.speaker: Player_Romus
117.text: "I'm listening. Tell me what you want."

118.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
118.text: "Power isn't the end goal. Justice is."

119.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
119.text: "The people have seen enough to know what real freedom looks like..."

121.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
121.text: "But now it’s falling apart. Stability built on injustice can’t last forever."

122.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
122.text: "You think the people will wait much longer for promises of reform? They’re already in the streets, Your Majesty."

123.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
123.text: "How can you say that when your own people have taken to the streets in open defiance of your authority?"

124.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
124.text: "You are the last obstacle standing in this country's way."

125.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
125.text: "I simply prefer to stand when I speak for the people."

126.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
126.text: "Instead of focusing on symbols of power, Your Excellency..."

127.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
127.text: "...Would you be kind enough to tell me what you intend to achieve by summoning me here?"

128.speaker: Player_Romus
128.text: "And that's why I'm here. To talk."

131.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
131.text: "I thought you were aware of my position."

132.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
132.text: "Seeing as how I've been summoned here as your guest, perhaps you'd be kind enough to tell me what you intend to achieve today?"

133.speaker: Player_Romus
133.text: "Mr. Sazon told me you're not willing to compromise on reforms, and instead want me to abdicate. Is that true?"

137.speaker: Player_Romus
137.text: "I called you here because there’s still time to prevent this from spiraling out of control."

138.speaker: Player_Romus
138.text: "What I intend to achieve, Mr. Sotelato, is to avoid an unmitigated disaster."

139.speaker: Player_Romus
139.text: "You're harnessing the anger of the people, but anger doesn't build nations. I summoned you because of your influence, but I need to know if you have a vision beyond destruction."

140.speaker: Player_Romus
140.text: "I just wanted to see for myself who you really are."

142.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
142.text: "Sazon had his way of thinking, and it didn't work. He believed in half-measures, in preserving what no longer serves the people."

143.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
143.text: "Thousands are out in the streets as we speak. Because they now know the monarchy can’t be reformed. It needs to be dismantled."

144.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
144.text: "Anything less is just prolonging the inevitable."

148.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
148.text: "Then give the people what they want, and there won't be a disaster."

149.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
149.text: "Just look at the chaos in the streets. Disaster is already upon us, regardless of your willingness to see it."

150.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
150.text: "The spiral started long ago. People don’t rise up overnight."

151.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
151.text: "If you truly want to stop this, then meet your people's demands. Otherwise, you've already lost control."

152.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
152.text: "Anger may not build nations, but it clears the way for something new."

153.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
153.text: "Our vision is to build a fair and just society. And such a change has to come from the people."

154.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
154.text: "But most importantly, the people need to know if *you* have the vision to listen and let go of power."

155.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
155.text: "And? Do you see a man, or a threat?"

156.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
156.text: "Thousands are marching for their rights as we speak. Because they now know the monarchy can’t be reformed. It needs to be dismantled."

157.speaker: Player_Romus
157.text: "Thousands on the streets may seem like a victory to you, but it's nothing to me. If you think your mob is immune from the Crown's justice, you're living in a fantasy."

158.speaker: Player_Romus
158.text: "Perhaps you’re right. Maybe the time of monarchies has passed. If the people no longer believe in the Crown, then what’s left of it?"

159.speaker: Player_Romus
159.text: "I'm not blind to the unrest. But dismantling the monarchy isn't the solution."

161.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
161.text: "This isn't about me. It’s the people's courage that drives this movement. Any one of them could be standing here in my stead."

162.speaker: Player_Romus
162.text: "But they're not. You are the one who must face the full weight of the Crown’s justice."

163.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
163.text: "Then you know what needs to happen."

165.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
165.text: "Superficial reforms to keep the masses in check while the Crown keeps enjoying its privileges?"

169.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
169.text: "That's no longer a possibility. You didn't even accept our demands for reform."

170.speaker: Player_Romus
170.text: "I actually think it is about you, Adarfo. Are you really saying everyone in this so-called movement wants the kingdom gone, and you are merely their mouthpiece?"

171.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
171.text: "More fake promises? You clearly never intended to follow up with the reforms you and Manus Sazon discussed."

175.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
175.text: "More oppression? You clearly never even wanted to listen to the call for reform."
175.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_TalkToAdarfo_AskedManus"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reforms_DiscussedOnYacht"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.HouseOfDelegates_Abolished"] == false)

179.speaker: Narrator
179.text: He narrowed his eyes and didn't respond for a while.

181.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
181.text: "A complete removal of citizens' rights? You abolished the House of Delegates, taking away the only political representation commoners had."
181.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_TalkToAdarfo_AskedManus"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reforms_DiscussedOnYacht"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.HouseOfDelegates_Abolished"] == false) == false)

182.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
182.text: "How far do you have to go until enough is enough?"

183.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
183.text: "And now, it's perfectly clear to the Rizian people that the obstacle before them is this very institution you hold dear, and that crown you wear."

187.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
187.text: "And what happened to Mr. Sazon, who thought he could compromise with his noble peers? His half-measures and moderate views couldn't save him."

188.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
188.text: "If you're willing to step aside peacefully, you can still help shape the future of this nation, rather than be swept away by it."

189.speaker: Player_Romus
189.text: "We've seen what happens when revolutions promise freedom. They leave nothing but rubble behind."

190.speaker: Player_Romus
190.text: "Before we continue, why don't you sit down? We’re both here to discuss Rizia's future."

191.speaker: Player_Romus
191.text: "Really? I think it looks rather nice."

193.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
193.text: "An open field where healthy, well-fed children play. A factory owned and operated by the workers themselves. An apartment block whose residents don't have to struggle to pay their rent anymore."

194.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
194.text: "The system is already rubble. And it's crumbling further under the weight of inequality and greed."

195.speaker: Narrator
195.text: For a moment he seemed noticeably agitated, before he took a deep breath and continued.

196.speaker: Player_Romus
196.text: "I see nobody. And nobody will ever see you again. GUARDS!"

197.speaker: Player_Romus
197.text: "I see both. A man with conviction, and a threat to this country's order."

198.speaker: Player_Romus
198.text: "I see a man who believes in his cause, and maybe he is right to believe in it."

199.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
199.text: "Thousands are marching for this cause as we speak. Because they now know the monarchy can’t be reformed. It needs to be dismantled."

200.speaker: Player_Romus
200.text: "I see a man who's stirring up unrest in order to catapult himself into power."

201.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
201.text: "The threat to this country is the handful of people who hold all the power. Yourself included."

202.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
202.text: "You're too used to things being done top-to-bottom that you cannot comprehend people organizing themselves."

203.speaker: Player_Romus
203.text: "You look troubled, Adarfo. I hope you didn't underestimate the situation you walked into."

204.speaker: Player_Romus
204.text: "What's the matter? Lost for words? It’s easy to talk of revolution, but when faced with the reality of power, things become much less poetic, don't they?"

205.speaker: Player_Romus
205.text: "...But we don't want that to happen now, do we?"

207.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
207.text: "Maybe you think the ‘Crown's justice’ is enough to keep the people in line, but they're past the point of fear."

208.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
208.text: "No, we don't. But what you fail to see is that this isn't about what you or I want anymore."

209.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
209.text: "I don't think this is the time for you to throw around threats."
209.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Manus_Arrested"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Manus_SendToWar"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Manus_Gone"] == true) == false)

210.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
210.text: "You think I'm afraid? The people are beyond fear, and so am I. It's not me you should worry about."

214.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
214.text: "Mr. Sazon said you might be open to the idea. Though I doubted him, I came to see for myself."

215.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
215.text: "Are you willing to do that, Your Majesty?"

216.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
216.text: "I will not betray their trust by tempering my words. We can work together, or we can oppose each other. I will not compromise the truth of what needs to be done."

217.speaker: Player_Romus
217.text: "I don't like your attitude, Mr. Sotelato. I advise you to watch your mouth."

218.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
218.text: "And I ask you to consider why my attitude is the way it is, Your Majesty. I'm not here to placate or to play politics. I'm here because the people demand change."

219.speaker: Player_Romus
219.text: "Oh, please. Rizia remains one of the wealthiest countries in Southern Merkopa."

226.speaker: Player_Romus
226.text: "Who is suffering? Nobody suffers in Rizia."

227.speaker: Player_Romus
227.text: "Our citizens are enjoying some of the best living standards in all of eastern Merkopa."

228.speaker: Player_Romus
228.text: "Watch what you say. Living standards in Rizia are still higher than in most of the world."
228.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Great"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Good"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Average"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Acceptable"] == true)

232.speaker: Player_Romus
232.text: "What are you talking about? Rizia has strong protections for workers' rights."

233.speaker: Player_Romus
233.text: "You and I want the same thing, Mr. Sotelato. I suggest you take a moment to calm down."

235.speaker: Narrator
235.text: He waited for me to continue.

236.speaker: Player_Romus
236.text: "I want to work with you. The monarchy's end is near. If the people no longer believe in the crown, then what’s left of it?"

237.speaker: Player_Romus
237.text: "I want to avoid a disaster on the streets. So I want you to listen to me."

238.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
238.text: "No, Your Majesty. It's you who need to listen to the people."

239.speaker: Player_Romus
239.text: "You are a problem, Adarfo. I'm afraid you must face the full justice of the Crown."

242.speaker: Narrator
242.text: The door swung open so fast it nearly came off its hinges. With a loud commotion, Titus and his men rushed in and surrounded the revolutionary.

243.speaker: Player_Romus
243.text: "I might be willing to step aside, but dismantling the monarchy sounds too extreme."

244.speaker: Player_Romus
244.text: "It's not as simple as 'stepping aside.' If I abdicate without appointing a successor, the other Houses will try to take the Crown for themselves. You know that."

245.speaker: Player_Romus
245.text: "If I do this, there must be a plan. I can't let chaos fill the power vacuum."

246.speaker: Player_Romus
246.text: "I've ruled long enough to know when the winds of change are too strong to resist. I'm willing to cede power to your movement, but I need to have your trust first."

247.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
247.text: "You just said it yourself. The time of monarchies has passed. People will not accept any successor to your rule."

249.speaker: Player_Romus
249.text: "Let's say I am. How do you plan to abolish the monarchy?"

250.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
250.text: "Of course, it won't be that simple."

252.speaker: Player_Romus
252.text: "You know what? Forget about it. Our meeting is over."

254.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
254.text: "The nobility won't give up their claim to power without a fight. We need to ensure that this transition doesn't turn into a battle for the throne."

264.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
264.text: "Go ahead and put me in jail alongside Manus  Sazon. You’d only be adding fuel to the fire."

265.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
265.text: "Go ahead and send me to die like you did with Manus Sazon. You’d only be adding fuel to the fire."
265.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Manus_Arrested"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Manus_SendToWar"] == true) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Manus_DiesInWar"] == true)

269.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
269.text: "Go ahead and send me to war like Manus Sazon. You’d only be adding fuel to the fire."
269.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Manus_Arrested"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Manus_SendToWar"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Manus_DiesInWar"] == true) == false)

270.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
270.text: "Manus Sazon might have abandoned the cause, but I will not. I am not a son of a noble or an aristocrat."
270.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Manus_Arrested"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Manus_SendToWar"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Manus_Gone"] == true)

278.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
278.text: "And now he rots in jail. Just because he advocated for people's rights."

279.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
279.text: "You sent him to die in your unjustified war. Because he advocated for people's rights."

280.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
280.text: "You made him disappear. Because he advocated for people's rights."

286.speaker: Player_Romus
286.text: "Look. I want to make peace with the protesters. Can you help me with that or not?"

287.speaker: Player_Romus
287.text: "I'm not blind to the unrest. But dismantling the monarchy isn't the solution."

288.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
288.text: "I just told you what you need to do to make peace with the protesters. Step aside and help them dismantle the monarchy."

289.speaker: Player_Romus
289.text: "I'm open to discussing reforms. I’d even consider abdicating in favor of my daughter, who supports your cause. Surely we can find a middle ground."

297.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
297.text: "I'm afraid it's too late for that."

298.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
298.text: "You had the time and the means to reform the country but you choose not to."
298.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.HouseOfDelegates_Abolished"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_TalkToAdarfo_AskedManus"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_Hostage"] == true) == false)

299.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
299.text: "Your idea of 'reform' was to abolish the House of Delegates. How can we compromise after that?"
299.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.HouseOfDelegates_Abolished"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_TalkToAdarfo_AskedManus"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_Hostage"] == true) == false)

302.speaker: Player_Romus
302.text: "Manus Sazon chose to fight for his country."

304.speaker: Player_Romus
304.text: "Perhaps you’re right. Maybe the time for the monarchy has passed. If the people no longer believe in the Crown, then what’s left of it?"

305.speaker: Player_Romus
305.text: "Perhaps I will. Perhaps the time for monarchies has passed."

308.speaker: Player_Romus
308.text: "I understand the situation and I'm open for a possible cooperation."

310.speaker: Player_Romus
310.text: "They believe that because you have convinced them of it. But you won't have influence over them for long."

312.speaker: Player_Romus
312.text: "The time for monarchies may have passed, but I won't hand the keys of power to a mob of revolutionaries."

313.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
313.text: "That's why the people need to take control of this process through a renewed parliament -- a transitionary government -- that strips the royal houses of their leverage over Rizia."

314.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
314.text: "Unlike the House of Delegates of today, this 'People's Assembly,' if you will, must be composed exclusively of working-class and common citizens."

315.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
315.text: "If the King gives his support to the movement and its vision for the nation, it will be possible to have a smooth transition."

316.speaker: Player_Romus
316.text: "And what will this 'renewed' parliament look like?"

317.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
317.text: "As the basis for this transitionary government, they'll be tasked with drafting a new constitution. One that guarantees the redistribution of land, wealth, and power."

318.speaker: Player_Romus
318.text: "You say the nobles will lose their leverage. How do you intend to disarm them, politically as well as literally?"

319.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
319.text: "Their political power will be dismantled through legal reforms made by the transitionary government."

320.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
320.text: "All noble houses will be stripped of their titles and influence. Their massive estates will be nationalized and put to use for the people. They will hold no special privileges, no control over land or resources."

321.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
321.text: "Their provincial militaries and police forces will immediately be disbanded. Of course, we will need to form our own security forces to oversee this."

322.speaker: Player_Romus
322.text: "And what role do you expect me to play in this?"

323.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
323.text: "You must show the people that even the monarchy understands when its time has come."

324.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
324.text: "Your endorsement of the new government is critical for preventing bloodshed and chaos. You'd be setting an example for future revolutions across the globe."

325.speaker: Player_Romus
325.text: "What if some of the nobles attempt to rally their forces before you even begin the transition?"

326.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
326.text: "We are already prepared for that risk. The revolutionary movement already has the support of many workers' groups and local militias."

327.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
327.text: "But to ensure a stable transition, we must strike before they do."

328.speaker: Player_Romus
328.text: "The Royal Houses will never wait for your reforms to be implemented. They will strike before you can put your new government in place."

345.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
345.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.TalkWithAdarfo_NewGovernment_Set1_Option1"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.TalkWithAdarfo_NewGovernment_Set1_Option2"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.TalkWithAdarfo_NewGovernment_Set1_Option3"] == true) == false

350.speaker: Player_Romus
350.text: "I see what you're getting at... Go on."

351.speaker: Player_Romus
351.text: "And how do you want me to help you with that?"

353.speaker: Player_Romus
353.text: "I'm sorry, but I won't let you get away with such an action."

355.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
355.text: "It is exactly what this country needs."

357.speaker: Player_Romus
357.text: "What this country needs is fewer provocateurs like you. Guards!"

360.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
360.text: "Wait, Your Majesty. We can solve this without bloodshed."

363.speaker: Player_Romus
363.text: "You've just admitted to conspiring against the ruling government. GUARDS!"

365.speaker: Player_Romus
365.text: "I'm sorry. You forced me to do this. This meeting is over."

366.speaker: Player_Romus
366.text: "Enough, Sotelato. I want no part in this."

367.speaker: Player_Romus
367.text: "What *exactly* do you want me to do?"

368.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
368.text: "I'm aware of the upcoming gathering where the leaders of all the noble houses will convene in Porte Drazon to pay their respects to the Queen Mother."

369.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
369.text: "You must assure the nobility about the security situation and let the gathering proceed as planned."

370.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
370.text: "My forces will take care of the rest."

371.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
371.text: "Well... yes. Apologies to the Queen Mother, but it's not often that every high-ranking noble in Rizia gathers in one place."

372.speaker: Player_Romus
372.text: "All of my loved ones will be present at this gathering. Are you going to strike them, too?"

373.speaker: Player_Romus
373.text: "You're suggesting I use my mother's birthday to betray the entire Rizian nobility?"

374.speaker: Player_Romus
374.text: "And what happens if they resist? Do you plan to arrest the heads of every noble family? What happens next?"

375.speaker: Player_Romus
375.text: "How do you plan to get by the Golden Guard? Do you think they'll just open the door for you?"

385.speaker: Player_Romus
385.text: "Hmm. I like the sound of that."

390.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
390.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.TalkWithAdarfo_NewGovernment_Set2_Option1"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.TalkWithAdarfo_NewGovernment_Set2_Option2"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.TalkWithAdarfo_NewGovernment_Set2_Option3"] == true) == false

391.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
391.text: "A rare opportunity has been granted to us. We'd be fools not to seize it."

392.speaker: Player_Romus
392.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.TalkWithAdarfo_NewGovernment_Set2_Option1"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.TalkWithAdarfo_NewGovernment_Set2_Option2"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.TalkWithAdarfo_NewGovernment_Set2_Option3"] == true) == false

393.speaker: Narrator
393.text: He looked at me in anticipation.

395.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
395.text: "Great to hear. Do you have any questions before we move on?"

396.speaker: Player_Romus
396.text: "No. I get what the plan entails."

398.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
398.text: "If any of them resist, they’ll be subdued. But the goal is to make it clear that their power is finished."

399.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
399.text: "They will be given a choice -- relinquish their titles peacefully and support the new government, or face trial for their crimes."

400.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
400.text: "If you help us get our people inside the Royal Library, we can execute this swiftly and without violence."

401.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
401.text: "Our revolutionary forces will have the building surrounded, and additional units will be stationed at key points across Porte Drazon."

402.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
402.text: "You might be surprised to hear that we have the capacity to execute such an attack. But of course, if we move without your support, we risk a violent confrontation..."

403.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
403.text: "The Golden Guard is loyal to the Crown. We cannot guarantee they will stand down, even if the King orders them to do so. But if we know their security plans, we can enter the building without much resistance."

407.speaker: Player_Romus
407.text: "How can I help your strike go as planned?"

409.speaker: Player_Romus
409.text: "You can count on me, but you underestimate the Golden Guard. I won't be able to stop Titus and his men from killing every last one of you."

411.speaker: Player_Romus
411.text: "No. I'm afraid not. There will be no collaboration between us."

415.speaker: Player_Romus
415.text: "You heard me. This meeting is over."

416.speaker: Player_Romus
416.text: "I'm afraid there won't be any collaboration between us. You pushed your luck too much."

418.speaker: Player_Romus
418.text: "What I'm saying, Adarfo, is that I cannot simply let you go free after all of this."

426.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
426.text: "There is no need for that sort of talk."

428.speaker: Player_Romus
428.text: "Perhaps you're right... The time for the monarchies may have passed."

431.speaker: Player_Romus
431.text: "Better yet, I'll send you to prison. GUARDS!"

432.speaker: Player_Romus
432.text: "Your revolution will never succeed with you in prison. GUARDS!"

435.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
435.text: "I don't expect you to do so. All we need to know is where your guards will be at what time."

436.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
436.text: "It would be an immense help if you gave us access to the security plans and the layout of the library."

438.speaker: Player_Romus
438.text: "No, you won't. Not after the venom you’ve spewed today."

439.speaker: Player_Romus
439.text: "I'm afraid you are not going anywhere, Adarfo. You made a mistake by showing up here in the first place."

440.speaker: Player_Romus
440.text: "Regardless, it was nice to speak with you."

441.speaker: Player_Romus
441.text: "Be careful out there, Adarfo. I'll be watching you."

442.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
442.text: "The guards stationed at the entrance and other key points will be our primary concern. Once we know their positions, we can replace them swiftly."

443.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
443.text: "Alternately, you can help us insert our operatives into the event staff -- disguised as servers, attendants, caterers if needed. When the time comes, they will already be in place."

444.speaker: Player_Romus
444.text: "No, that's too complicated. I'll request a copy of the security plans from Titus and make sure it reaches you."

445.speaker: Player_Romus
445.text: "I'll try to get you inside as staff. Leave it up to me."

447.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
447.text: "You will ignite the flames of rebellion, Your Majesty."

455.speaker: Narrator
455.text: He turned and left without saying anything else.

456.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
456.text: "Thank you for having me, Your Majesty."

459.speaker: Player_Romus
459.text: "No. I’ll snuff them out once and for all."

461.speaker: Player_Romus
461.text: "I can't attempt any of that without raising suspicion. There must be another way."

462.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
462.text: "Then we'll strike with the means at our disposal."

464.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
464.text: "So be it, Your Majesty. You've earned my respect."

467.speaker: Player_Romus
467.text: "No, that is too risky. I'm afraid I've changed my mind about our cooperation."

469.speaker: Player_Romus
469.text: "All right, I'll do what I can to get you inside. But I can't promise you anything."

470.speaker: Player_Romus
470.text: "If this is your decision, I will not stand in your way."

473.speaker: Player_Romus
473.text: "Good. I've been dying for an excuse to show your rabble-rousers the full meaning of Rizian justice."

474.speaker: Player_Romus
474.text: "You're bluffing, Adarfo. Stop this unrest nonsense, and I might be persuaded to show you mercy."

479.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
479.text: "Imprisoning me will not silence the revolution. Deep down, you know that."

480.speaker: Player_Romus
480.text: "Fine. Leave immediately before I change my mind."

483.speaker: Player_Romus
483.text: "This man is conspiring against the nation of Rizia and its monarchy. I want him behind bars."

484.speaker: Player_Romus
484.text: "Mr. Sotelato shall not face any trials. He will be sent to prison to await his execution for his crimes against the Kingdom of Rizia."

488.speaker: Player_Romus
488.text: "I don't even care if you've done anything wrong or not. I just don't like your face."

489.speaker: Narrator
489.text: He did not resist, nor did he respond as the guards handcuffed him and led him outside.

490.speaker: Narrator
490.text: As I watched him get dragged away, I thought about his words.

495.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
495.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionMonarchy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionDemocratic"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionMilitaristic"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionNormal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionTheocratic"] == true

496.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
496.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionMonarchy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionDemocratic"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionMilitaristic"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionNormal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionTheocratic"] == true) == false

497.speaker: Player_Romus
497.text: "Thank you, Titus. I have settled on a direction."
497.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionMonarchy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionDemocratic"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionMilitaristic"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionNormal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionTheocratic"] == true

498.speaker: Narrator
498.text: He stopped walking. We had reached the doors to the room where Adarfo Sotelato had been instructed to wait.

500.speaker: Player_Romus
500.text: "Tell the artist to paint the Queen Mother as she really is."

501.speaker: Player_Romus
501.text: "I want a portrait depicting Mother as the champion of the common people. The more sympathetic, the better."

502.speaker: Player_Romus
502.text: "He should make it as regal as possible, befitting the matriarch of House Toras. Perhaps real gold could be used in the paint?"

503.speaker: Player_Romus
503.text: "She must be portrayed as a symbol of strength and valor, embodying the spirit of our victorious forces."

504.speaker: Player_Romus
504.text: "Something spiritual and awe-inspiring is the way to go. I want it to bring Wruhecists to their knees."

505.speaker: Titus Gordion
505.text: "I will relay the directions immediately. It will undoubtedly be a masterpiece."

513.speaker: Titus Gordion
513.text: "Good luck, Your Majesty. My men and I will be right outside in case the rebel causes trouble."

515.speaker: Player_Romus
515.text: "People should see the portrait and be reminded of the strength and resilience of the Crown."

516.speaker: Player_Romus
516.text: "I want something that will appeal to the common people. As if she were not only Queen Mother, but mother to all."

517.speaker: Player_Romus
517.text: "Nothing too fancy. This is my mother we're talking about."

518.speaker: Player_Romus
518.text: "She should be seen as a holy figure. The mother who birthed our great Wruhecist kingdom."

519.speaker: Player_Romus
519.text: "We need a fearsome portrayal, one that intimidates and inspires in equal measure."

520.speaker: Titus Gordion
520.text: "Any Wruhecist royal would be honored to receive such a portrayal."

521.speaker: Titus Gordion
521.text: "But, as we both know, your mother is not a Wruhecist."

522.speaker: Titus Gordion
522.text: "She is still the Queen Mother of Rizia. Appropriate tribute must be paid, don't you think?"

523.speaker: Titus Gordion
523.text: "But of course, you know Madam Estela best."

524.speaker: Titus Gordion
524.text: "From what I can tell, Madam Estela distanced herself from her commoner roots long ago."

525.speaker: Titus Gordion
525.text: "Such a portrait could appeal to populists, but remind the nobility of the scandal that almost cost your father the crown."

526.speaker: Titus Gordion
526.text: "Yes, that would suit her legacy well, reaffirming House Toras' rule."

527.speaker: Titus Gordion
527.text: "Although I would caution against her appearing too high and mighty. You want viewers to feel a connection, not reverence alone."

528.speaker: Titus Gordion
528.text: "I like the idea of reinforcing our kingdom's strength through the portrait, Your Majesty."

529.speaker: Titus Gordion
529.text: "That said, I find it hard to imagine Madame Estela as much of a warrior."

551.speaker: Narrator
551.text: I walked through the bustling hallways of Palas Rezna, on my way to the conference room, where I would meet Adarfo Sotelato.

552.speaker: Narrator
552.text: The event was set to take place in the Grand Library of Porte Drazon, soon to be renamed in her honor.

553.speaker: Narrator
553.text: Preparations for my mother’s 75th birthday celebrations were in full swing, bringing together all of Rizia’s noble houses for the occasion.

554.speaker: Narrator
554.text: With the event a month away and the library renovations far from complete, the tension in the air was palpable.

558.speaker: Titus Gordion
558.text: "Mr. Adria asked me to inform you that he’s just commissioned a painter for the Queen Mother’s birthday portrait."

559.speaker: Titus Gordion
559.text: "The artist wants to know how Madam Estela should be portrayed."

566.speaker: Titus Gordion
566.text: "Your new head butler has asked me to inform you that he’s just commissioned a painter for the Queen Mother’s birthday portrait."

571.speaker: Titus Gordion
571.text: "Though we both know your mother is not an avid sanctuary-goer. I never see her at services."

575.speaker: Narrator
575.text: Sotelato was standing beside the entrance as I stepped inside.

576.speaker: Player_Romus
576.text: "Sounds great. Why don't you throw in a few fairies and talking dogs while you're at it?"

580.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
580.text: "Besides, do you even know whether or not your daughter is alive?"

584.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
584.text: "Your daughter had the good sense to escape your regime. She knew what was coming."

588.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
588.text: "Unlike the former House of Delegates, this 'People's Assembly,' if you will, must be composed exclusively of working-class and common citizens."

592.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
592.text: "Their provincial police forces will immediately be disbanded. Of course, we will need to form our own security forces to oversee this."
592.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Order_RemoveProvincialPolice"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Order_RemoveProvincialLevies"] == false) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Order_RemoveProvincialPolice"] == false)

599.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
599.text: "Their provincial militaries will immediately be disbanded. Of course, we will need to form our own security forces to oversee this."
599.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Order_RemoveProvincialPolice"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Order_RemoveProvincialLevies"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Order_RemoveProvincialPolice"] == false) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Order_RemoveProvincialLevies"] == false)

600.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
600.text: "With their provincial militaries and police forces disbanded, it will be difficult for them to fight back. Nonetheless, we will need to form our own security forces to deal with potential resistance."
600.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Order_RemoveProvincialPolice"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Order_RemoveProvincialLevies"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Order_RemoveProvincialPolice"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Order_RemoveProvincialLevies"] == false) == false)

601.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
601.text: "The revolutionary movement already has the support of many workers' groups and local militias. We are prepared for this."

602.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
602.text: "I promise no one will be harmed. But you'll have time to get your family members out of the library before we act, if you wish."

608.speaker: Narrator
608.text: Had I extinguished the fires of rebellion? Or would they burn higher in Adarfo's absence?

609.speaker: Narrator
609.text: He reached out his hand to me.

610.speaker: Player_Romus
610.text: "If I don't get a bow, you don't get a handshake."

612.speaker: Player_Romus
612.text: "I am with you, my brother. For the revolution."

617.speaker: Narrator
617.text: He looked slightly confused, but nodded.

618.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
618.text: "Thank you once again for meeting me. We will see each other soon."

619.speaker: Narrator
619.text: He pushed the door open and walked out without another word.

620.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
620.text: "A handshake is a gesture between equals, whereas... never mind. Soon enough, it won't matter."

621.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
621.text: "They've seen enough to know what real freedom looks like..."

622.speaker: Narrator
622.text: I paused for a moment, considering how to get the security plans for the gathering from Titus without arousing his suspicion.

623.speaker: Narrator
623.text: After Adarfo's departure, Titus approached me.

624.speaker: Titus Gordion
624.text: "I hope the meeting went well, Your Majesty. That man is trouble."

625.speaker: Player_Romus
625.text: "He is an interesting fellow to say the least."

626.speaker: Player_Romus
626.text: "To be honest, I couldn't care less about that commoner."

628.speaker: Titus Gordion
628.text: "I was under the impression that you were interested in talking to him, Your Majesty."

629.speaker: Player_Romus
629.text: "It went well, Titus, but I'm currently thinking more about my mother's birthday to be honest."

630.speaker: Player_Romus
630.text: "He is trouble, I'll give you that... Speaking of which, have you had a chance to update the security protocols for the birthday? I'd like to review them to ensure we're fully prepared."

633.speaker: Titus Gordion
633.text: "I can give you a general overview, but the specific security details are sensitive and meant only for the Guard’s knowledge -- for your own safety."

634.speaker: Titus Gordion
634.text: "We've modified the security protocols to realign certain entry and exit points. As always, the Golden Guard will ensure the highest level of protection."

635.speaker: Titus Gordion
635.text: "I'm sure she’ll be pleased, Your Majesty."

636.speaker: Player_Romus
636.text: "Given the importance of the attendees, it's essential for me to be fully informed. The safety of everyone at the gathering, including my mother and myself, is at stake."

637.speaker: Player_Romus
637.text: "I'm not doubting your capabilities, Titus. I just wanted to go over them with you."

638.speaker: Player_Romus
638.text: "I understand, Titus. I trust you have everything under control."

639.speaker: Player_Romus
639.text: "I'd like to review those 'realignments.' I want to ensure there are no blind spots that may have been have overlooked."

640.speaker: Player_Romus
640.text: "Speaking of the birthday, the fact that we'll be outside the palace changes things. Have you ensured every entry and exit point is covered?"

641.speaker: Player_Romus
641.text: "She probably won’t even notice the details, but it'll be a fine tribute."

642.speaker: Player_Romus
642.text: "Oh, It was Hugo's idea. Why would I want to meet with this guy otherwise?"

643.speaker: Player_Romus
643.text: "Given the meteoric surge in his popularity, I just wanted to see the man for myself."

648.speaker: Player_Romus
648.text: "I was. Until I realized I don't care about him or his views."

650.speaker: Player_Romus
650.text: "It's my mother's birthday, Titus. It's only natural that I'd want to be fully informed."

651.speaker: Player_Romus
651.text: "Good. I expect the security plans on my desk by tomorrow."

655.speaker: Player_Romus
655.text: "Last I checked, it wasn't in your job purview to concern yourself with such matters."

656.speaker: Titus Gordion
656.text: "I assure you, the Golden Guard will ensure the protection of everyone attending, Your Majesty. You really don't have anything to worry about."

657.speaker: Titus Gordion
657.text: "I will provide you with the plans as soon as possible."

658.speaker: Titus Gordion
658.text: "Thank you for your time, Your Majesty."

659.speaker: Player_Romus
659.text: "Listen. I won't feel secure unless I understand the full extent of our defenses."

669.speaker: Player_Romus
669.text: "You're right. Thank you. Great job as always, Titus."

670.speaker: Player_Romus
670.text: "I think the threat is exaggerated. He is no trouble."

673.speaker: Player_Romus
673.text: "I just want to organize the best possible celebration for my mother, and I'm concerned our cooks here just won't do it."

674.speaker: Player_Romus
674.text: "I was just second guessing my choice about her portrait. I hope she likes it."

675.speaker: Player_Romus
675.text: "Is there, Titus? You tell me. Have you had a chance to update the security protocols for the birthday?"

676.speaker: Titus Gordion
676.text: "I wouldn't jump to that conclusion so quickly, sir."

677.speaker: Titus Gordion
677.text: "Do you think he is a threat?"

680.speaker: Titus Gordion
680.text: "Did you have something in mind, sir?"

681.speaker: Player_Romus
681.text: "No, not really. But speaking of the birthday, the fact that we'll be outside the palace changes things. Have you ensured every entry and exit point is covered?"

682.speaker: Player_Romus
682.text: "Yes. I want to bring in a special catering service for the birthday. I don't want to rely on the palace kitchens."

683.speaker: Player_Romus
683.text: "I was just wondering what you think."

684.speaker: Player_Romus
684.text: "That man is nothing but a threat."

685.speaker: Player_Romus
685.text: "He is just a romantic Malenyevist. We shouldn't worry about him."

686.speaker: Player_Romus
686.text: "Honestly, I'm not sure. But I did enjoy my little meeting with him."

687.speaker: Titus Gordion
687.text: "Should we have him watched more closely?"

688.speaker: Player_Romus
688.text: "No, I don't think that's really necessary."

689.speaker: Player_Romus
689.text: "Possibly. But not now, Titus. We have more important things like my mother's birthday that's coming up."

690.speaker: Player_Romus
690.text: "I thought he was already being watched *closely*."

691.speaker: Player_Romus
691.text: "Thanks for the advice, Titus. By the way, have you had a chance to update the security protocols for the birthday? I'd like to review them to ensure we're fully prepared."

693.speaker: Player_Romus
693.text: "You're right, Titus, but I'm currently thinking more about my mother's birthday to be honest."

702.speaker: Titus Gordion
702.text: "Broadly speaking, yes. However, you explicitly told the security forces not to intervene with his movement, Your Majesty. But I digress."

706.speaker: Titus Gordion
706.text: "The intelligence forces can always do more, but I digress."

709.speaker: Titus Gordion
709.text: "If you'll excuse me, I will now take my leave, sir."

712.speaker: Player_Romus
712.text: "Not really, but I have some concerns about the upcoming gathering."

713.speaker: Player_Romus
713.text: "There is, actually. I want to organize the best possible celebration for my mother, and I'm concerned our cooks here just won't do it. I want a change of staff."

714.speaker: Titus Gordion
714.text: "Uh, I'm not really in a position to give advice on matters like this, sir."

715.speaker: Titus Gordion
715.text: "But I wouldn't change any plans regarding the staff at this moment. It poses a security risk."

716.speaker: Player_Romus
716.text: "Yes. I need you to give me the security plans for my mother's birthday."

718.speaker: Titus Gordion
718.text: "I would advise against that, Your Majesty. We shouldn't involve any outsiders in such a delicate gathering."

719.speaker: Titus Gordion
719.text: "Is there anything else I can help you with, Your Majesty?"

732.speaker: Narrator
732.text: I watched him as he walked away as I thought about what was about to happen to Rizia.

733.speaker: Titus Gordion
733.text: "Besides, sir, I believe the cooks were hand-picked by the Queen Mother Estela herself. I imagine she would take pride in their work for such a special occasion."

734.speaker: Player_Romus
734.text: "My mother herself requested this, Titus. I trust you'll see to it."

735.speaker: Player_Romus
735.text: "This isn't just about my mother, Titus. I want to display my personal touch to the royal houses."

736.speaker: Player_Romus
736.text: "I appreciate your concerns, but this decision has already been made. I expect you to ensure the security of the catering staff and make sure they are allowed inside to oversee the service."

738.speaker: Titus Gordion
738.text: "Of course, Your Majesty. I'll see it done."

745.speaker: Titus Gordion
745.text: "The Queen Mother is 75. I hardly think a festiburu is appropriate."

746.speaker: Narrator
746.text: A festiburu was a traditional Rizian festive object filled with treats. Participants took turns striking it until it burst.

747.speaker: Titus Gordion
747.text: "Anyway, the portrait's a done deal. Your thoughts?"

749.speaker: Player_Romus
749.text: "I haven't decided yet. Would you mind if I ran a few ideas by you?"
